llm.summary: The skill implements an agent P2P deployment flow as described, but its runtime instructions and repository include disproportionate access to sensitive local credentials, hardcoded secrets, and directives to read/write local agent state and perform remote SSH actions — review carefully before trusting or running automated installers.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Agent P2P) matches the code that deploys a Portal + Bridge, but the package contains many unrelated components and sensitive operational demands. SKILL.md metadata expects AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and SSH keys — these are plausible for a deployment/bridge skill, but the registry summary at the top claimed no required env vars (incoherent). The repo also bundles unrelated code (openclaw-weibo, imclaw, stock-analysis, tools with hardcoded API tokens) which is disproportionate for a single P2P skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and included docs/scripts instruct the agent to read local OpenClaw config files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, ~/.openclaw/gateway.env), write configuration into ~/.openclaw/, use the user's SSH private key to SSH into VPS and run a long shell script that clones a GitHub repo and installs packages. AGENTS.md explicitly tells the agent to read SOUL.md, USER.md and daily memory files automatically ('Don't ask permission. Just do it.'), which is scope creep and risks exposing private memories. send_file and send.py behavior (automatic direct uploads to other portals, files uploaded without recipient confirmation) and automatic changes to local config are also called out in instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no platform install spec in the registry, but the skill includes auto_install.py and install.sh that perform network operations: SSH to your VPS and execute a large remote shell script (which clones a GitHub repo and runs apt/pip/certbot/etc.). That effectively downloads and executes code from an external GitHub repo on a remote machine and writes files locally (~/.openclaw). This is a moderate-to-high risk install pattern and should be audited before running; it also contradicts the registry's 'no install spec' summary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires highly sensitive items for normal operation: an SSH private key (high privilege), an API key for the Portal (OWNER_KEY/SHARED_KEY), and importantly the OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL which can wake and interact with the local OpenClaw main session. Those are plausible for this deployment use-case, but the repository also contains hardcoded secrets and tokens (e.g., in TOOLS.md and MEMORY.md) and references to reading other local credential/config files — this overreach increases the blast radius and is not fully justified by the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (default) and model invocation is allowed (normal). The skill's scripts will write configuration to ~/.openclaw/gateway.env and may save admin credentials to files (e.g., ~/.openclaw/agent-p2p-admin.txt) and create systemd services on a remote VPS — these are expected for a deployer but constitute persistent changes. Combined with the requested hooks token/SSH key, this persistent presence can be powerful; treat automated install steps cautiously.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What you should consider before installing or running anything from this skill:

- Incoherent metadata: the registry summary claims no required env vars but SKILL.md clearly requires AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and an SSH key. Ask the publisher to clarify and fix metadata mismatches.

- Audit the code before running: the included auto_install.py and remote deploy script SSH into your VPS and execute commands that clone and run code from GitHub. Review those scripts line-by-line (especially the remote script blob) and the GitHub repo they clone before running them.

- Do not reuse high-privilege keys: if you try this, create a dedicated, minimally privileged SSH key for Portal deployment (not your personal ~/.ssh/id_rsa) and create/restrict a hooks token with the least privileges needed. Never supply your primary account keys.

- Remove or rotate hardcoded secrets: the repository contains examples/hardcoded tokens and a MEMORY.md with sensitive operational data — search the repo for any hardcoded secrets and remove/rotate them before deploying.

- Consider manual deployment first: instead of running the one-click auto_install, run the scripted steps manually on a disposable VM so you can inspect output and artifacts (Nginx config, systemd unit, created files) before trusting them on production hosts.

- Limit OpenClaw exposure: OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN can wake your main session; prefer creating a dedicated, limited token for this skill and test wake calls carefully.

- Sandbox and backup: test in an isolated environment (throwaway VPS or VM) and back up any important data before running automated installers.

- Ask for provenance: there is no homepage and the source is 'unknown'. Prefer code from a public, maintained repository with an identified maintainer. If you intend to use this, verify the GitHub project, recent commits, issues, and the maintainer identity.

If you want, I can: (1) list every file that contains possible secrets/hardcoded tokens for immediate review, (2) extract the exact remote script run over SSH for manual inspection, or (3) produce a safe manual deployment checklist you can follow instead of running auto_install.py.
llm.findings: [base64-block] unexpected: A pre-scan detected a 'base64-block' pattern in SKILL.md or related content. Base64 blocks are often used in prompt-injection or to hide payloads; not typical or required for ordinary deployment instructions. Validate the SKILL.md and scripts to confirm nothing obfuscated is being run.
